subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the native PowerShell smoke lane include both `pnpm check:docs` and `pnpm build:strict-smoke` now, or should OpenClaw start with a narrower passing command set?
rationale: The requested direction fits test infrastructure priorities, but the chosen commands affect recurring Windows CI cost and the current candidate has a live proof blocker around `build:strict-smoke`.

options.title: Prove full smoke before merge
options.body: Keep both requested commands, but land only after the exact Windows `pwsh` lane passes and the PR links this canonical issue.

options.title: Start with narrower smoke
options.body: Land only the PowerShell commands that already pass, then track Windows build-smoke hardening separately.

options.title: Defer recurring coverage
options.body: Keep this issue open until runner budget and Windows build-smoke ownership are settled.

recommendation.title: Prove full smoke before merge
recommendation.body: Keep both requested commands, but land only after the exact Windows `pwsh` lane passes and the PR links this canonical issue.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent overlap across CI workflow stabilization and the PowerShell-safe docs tooling repair.
